documents.title: Late Order Definition
documents.body: An order is considered late when today's date is after its promised_delivery date and the order status is not 'delivered'. Orders on hold follow separate escalation rules.

documents.title: Shipping SLA
documents.body: Standard shipping: promised delivery is 5-7 business days from order creation. Express shipping: 1-2 business days. Carrier delays after ship date do not reset the promised delivery clock.

documents.title: Refund Policy
documents.body: Full refund within 30 days of order creation if not delivered. Partial refund for late delivery after 3+ days late if customer requests. Delivered orders are eligible for return within 14 days.

documents.title: QC Failure Escalation
documents.body: When a part fails QC, a quality ticket must be opened. Reworked parts require a second QC pass before allocation. Downstream orders may be delayed if rework exceeds 48 hours.

documents.title: Inventory Allocation Rules
documents.body: Orders in 'processing' require available inventory for all line items. If available is zero, the order waits for next_restock_date. Partial allocation is allowed only for non-critical parts marked in the catalog.

documents.title: Order Hold Policy
documents.body: Orders on hold cannot ship until hold_reason is resolved. Common reasons: payment_verification, fraud_review, address_confirmation. Support must update the customer within 24 hours.

documents.title: Escalation Matrix
documents.body: P1 tickets require fulfillment manager ownership. P2 tickets go to the assigned engineer. Lookup ticket owner via mcp_get_user after fetching the ticket.

documents.title: Part Traceability
documents.body: To explain part delays, retrieve the full event timeline with ops_get_part_history, then cross-reference active orders via ops_find_orders_by_part. Look for qc_failed, delay_logged, and rework_started events.
